summary: FFV1 is a lossless, intra-frame video encoding format, and this informational document defines versions 0, 1 and 3 of it. It is designed to compress video in many pixel formats efficiently. Compared to uncompressed video it saves storage and adds frame fixity and self-description, which makes it useful for preservation or as an intermediate format.

eli5.summary: Imagine packing a movie into a smaller box without losing even one tiny detail. FFV1 is a recipe for doing exactly that, so libraries can store old films safely and take up less room.

questions: how does lossless video compression work
subtitle: Lossless video compression that preserves every pixel perfectly

tldr.problem: Organizations need to store video without losing any detail, but uncompressed video takes enormous storage space.
tldr.mechanism: FFV1 is a lossless codec that compresses video frames by predicting pixel values from neighboring pixels and storing only the differences.
tldr.outcome: Video preservationists, archivists, and researchers can store video in a fraction of the space while keeping every bit intact.

facts.label: Color spaces
facts.value: YCbCr, RGB, grayscale, with optional transparency

today: FFV1 is an informational RFC documenting a widely-used open-source codec. It has become a standard for video preservation and is deployed in professional and archival workflows.

sections.title: Lossless Video Compression
sections.content:
This RFC defines FFV1, a lossless video encoding format designed for long-term preservation, scientific imaging, screen recording, and other uses where data loss is unacceptable. The document covers versions 0, 1, and 3 of FFV1. Version 0 was released in 2006, version 1 added support for higher bit depths in 2009, and version 3 added integrity checking and enhanced characteristics description in 2013.

FFV1 is intra-frame only, meaning each frame is compressed independently without referencing other frames. This makes it easier to seek into the file and to recover from errors, compared to inter-frame codecs like H.264 or VP9.
sections.eli5: FFV1 is a way to pack a movie so it takes up less space on your hard drive, but when you open it again, every pixel is exactly as it was. That makes it perfect for libraries and archives.

sections.title: How Prediction and Compression Work
sections.content:
FFV1 breaks each frame into planes (color components), lines, and individual samples (pixels or color values). For each sample, the codec predicts what the value will be based on neighboring samples using a median predictor. The median of three nearby sample values (the pixel to the left, the pixel above, and the diagonal pixel) is used as the prediction. Instead of storing the actual pixel value, FFV1 stores only the difference between the actual value and the predicted value.

These differences are then compressed using either range coding or Golomb-Rice coding, both context-adaptive techniques that adjust their compression strategy based on the patterns observed so far in the bitstream.
sections.eli5: To save space, FFV1 notices that pixels next to each other are usually similar. It guesses what a pixel will be based on its neighbors, then just stores how wrong the guess was. That number is much smaller.

sections.title: Color Space Flexibility
sections.content:
FFV1 supports both YCbCr (luma and chroma components) and RGB (red, green, blue) color spaces. In YCbCr mode, the format optionally includes Cb (blue-difference) and Cr (red-difference) planes and a transparency plane. In RGB mode, FFV1 can apply the JPEG 2000 Reversible Color Transform (RCT), which converts RGB to a modified YCbCr space that compresses more efficiently while being perfectly reversible.

The codec allows various pixel depths from 8 to 16 bits per sample, and supports chroma subsampling where the color components use lower resolution than the luminance, a technique common in video.
sections.eli5: Video can store color in different ways. FFV1 handles the main ones, from simple grayscale to full color with transparency, so it works with whatever format your camera or application uses.

sections.title: Range and Golomb-Rice Coding
sections.content:
FFV1 supports two primary coding modes. Range coding encodes symbols by maintaining a range of values and splitting it based on estimated probabilities; this mode typically achieves slightly better compression. Golomb-Rice coding uses variable-length codes tuned to match the distribution of sample differences.

Both modes are context-adaptive: they track statistics of previously coded values and adjust their probability estimates accordingly. The range coder can be initialized fresh with each frame (keyframe mode) or can carry state from frame to frame.
sections.eli5: Imagine trying to guess whether the next pixel will be bright or dark based on all the pixels you've already seen. FFV1 gets smarter as it compresses, learning patterns and using them to guess better.

sections.title: Verification and Integrity
sections.content:
FFV1 version 3 adds Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) data at multiple levels: in the configuration record, at the end of each slice (tile), and optionally in quantization tables. These checksums allow decoders to detect corrupted data and validate that the stored bitstream matches what was intended.

The document describes the frame structure, with frames broken into slices for parallel processing and error recovery. A corrupted slice can be skipped or concealed without affecting the entire frame.
sections.eli5: Modern FFV1 adds check numbers at the end of pieces of the video. If something gets corrupted, the decoder can spot it and try to fix or skip just that broken piece.

sections.title: Use in Preservation and Implementation
sections.content:
FFV1 has been adopted by video preservation organizations and broadcast archives. The most widely used implementation is in FFmpeg, the popular open-source multimedia framework. The codec is used in tools like MediaConch for compliance checking. FFV1 can be wrapped in Matroska, AVI, or other container formats.

Because FFV1 is intra-frame and self-describing (the bitstream includes parameters for color space, bit depth, and encoding mode), it is well-suited for long-term storage where future readers may need to decode files without relying on external metadata.
sections.eli5: Libraries, museums, and broadcasters use FFV1 to store precious videos, because it's open, it packs small, and it never loses quality. Popular software like FFmpeg can read and write it.
